Use case: ui-mockup. Generate a polished, exceptional art-directed restaurant QR-menu design proposal, NOT implementation. Landscape presentation image at highest practical resolution. Show exactly TWO fully readable flat UI screens on a neutral presentation canvas: a generous desktop browser layout on the LEFT occupying about 68% and a tall narrow MOBILE screen on the RIGHT occupying about 27%, separated by generous clean whitespace. Screen proportions realistic: desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844; no perspective, no glossy devices, no hands, no laptop desk. Both are the SAME concept responsive adaptation with intelligently different composition. Include a modest outside-screen board heading with concept number and name and page type. Restaurant placeholder brand is ZEEN. Turkish UI text must be short, real and legible; avoid gibberish and dense invented paragraphs. Design must feel buildable with HTML/CSS, have accessible contrasts, 44px mobile tap targets, natural scrolling, no interaction puzzle, no onboarding, no forced swipe, no advertising, no admin controls or theme selectors. No multiple alternative layouts within one screen. Photorealistic appetizing food imagery. Avoid stock SaaS bento UI, generic purple gradients, heavy drop shadows, excessive badges, duplicate CTAs, ornamental random symbols. This is a serious best-in-class creative proposal, originality and simplicity equally critical.
Board: "01 / SOFRA — KARŞILAMA".

Warm uncoated ivory, deep oxblood red, near-black editorial typography; elegant high-contrast serif headlines with very clean sans body. Fine hairline rules and generous whitespace, no gradients. Authentic overhead Turkish/Mediterranean breakfast photography on handmade ceramic plates. Asymmetric editorial composition, restrained oxblood restaurant seal; cultured but approachable.

Mobile: wordmark/language on top, headline above a beautiful cropped single breakfast plate filling the central 40%, primary button anchored comfortably near bottom; no cropped button. Optional tiny opening hours as quiet footer. No food list, no menu grid here.
